sanskrit: jyotiṣmantaṃ sukṛtāṃ lokam īpsan pañcaudanaṃ brahmaṇe 'jaṃ dadāti | sa vyāpnuhy abhi lokaṃ jayāsmai śivo 'smabhyaṃ pratigṛhīta edhi ||
english: Desiring the luminous world of the well-doers, he gives the goat along with the five-grain offering to the brahmin. May he pervade and win the world for this man; be gracious to us, O received gift, come.

sanskrit: ajas trināke tridive tripṛṣṭhe sukṛtāṃ loke dadivāṃsaṃ dadhāti | pañcaudano brahmaṇe dīyamānaḥ sa dātāraṃ tṛptyā tarpayāsi ||
english: The goat establishes the giver in the triple firmament, the triple heaven, the triple ridge, in the world of the well-doers. The five-grain offering, being given to the brahmin, satisfies the giver with fullness.

sanskrit: ajo hy agner ajaniṣṭa śokād vipro viprasya sahaso vayodhāḥ | hutam iṣṭam abhipūrtaṃ vaṣaṭkṛtaṃ tad devā ṛtuśaḥ kalpayantu ||
english: For the goat was born from the flame of Agni, a sage born of the sage, the mighty one, the life-bearer. May the gods, in due season, accomplish that which has been offered, sacrificed, fulfilled, and consecrated with vaṣaṭ.

sanskrit: amotaṃ vāso dadhyād dhiraṇyam api dakṣiṇām | tathā lokān samāpnuyād ye divyā ye ca pārthivāḥ ||
english: He should add woven cloth, gold, and also the sacrificial fee. Thus may he attain all the worlds, those that are celestial and those that are earthly.

sanskrit: etās tvāja dhārā upa yantu viśvataḥ somyā devīr ghṛtapṛṣṭhā madhuścutaḥ | stabhāna pṛthivīṃ divaṃ sacasva nāke tiṣṭhāsy adhi saptaraśmau ||
english: May these streams, O goat, approach you from all sides — divine, rich in soma, bearing ghee on their backs, dripping with honey. Propping up the earth, accompany heaven; you stand on the firmament, upon the seven-rayed one.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhāt pṛthivyā iti catasraḥ ||
english: [The rubric:] "From the back of the earth" — thus the four [verses are recited].

sanskrit: pañcaudanaṃ pañcabhir aṅgulībhir darvyod dhara pañcadhaudanam etam | prācīṃ diśaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ pratīcīm udīcīṃ dhruvām ūrdhvāṃ diśam ā kramasva ||
english: Lift up this five-grain offering with five fingers in the ladle; divide this offering fivefold. Stride forth to the eastern quarter, to the southern, the western, the northern, the fixed, and the upward direction.

sanskrit: prācyāṃ diśi śiro ajasya dhehi dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi dakṣiṇaṃ dhehi pārśvam | pratīcyāṃ diśi bhasadam asya udīcyāṃ diśy uttaraṃ dhehi pārśvam ||
english: Place the head of the goat in the eastern direction; place its right flank in the southern direction. Place its hindquarters in the western direction; place its left flank in the northern direction.

sanskrit: ajasyānūkam ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi dhehi diśi dhehi pājasyaṃ dhruvāyām | antarikṣe madhyato madhyam asya padbhiś caturbhiḥ prati tiṣṭha dikṣu ||
english: Place the backbone of the goat in the upward direction; place its leg-joint in the fixed direction. Its middle part, in the atmosphere at the center — stand firm in the directions with your four feet.

sanskrit: śṛtam ajaṃ śṛtayā prorṇuhi tvacā sarvair aṅgaiḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ viśvarūpam | sa ut tiṣṭha prehi nākam uttamaṃ padbhiś caturbhiḥ prati tiṣṭha dikṣu ||
english: Cover the cooked goat with its own cooked skin, assembled with all its limbs, of all-encompassing form. Rise up, go forth to the highest firmament; stand firm in the directions with your four feet.

sanskrit: sarvā diśaḥ saṃvidānāḥ sadhrīcīḥ sāntardeśāḥ prati gṛhṇantu tejasam | te rakṣantu tava tubhyam etaṃ tābhyo juhomi haviṣā ghṛtena ||
english: May all the directions, in agreement, aligned, together with the intermediate regions, receive the radiance. May they guard this offering of yours, for you; I pour oblation to them with the sacrificial offering and with ghee.

sanskrit: yaṃ brāhmaṇe nidadhe yaṃ ca vikṣu yā vipruṣa odanānām ajasya | sarvaṃ tad agne sukṛtasya loke jānītān naḥ saṃgamane pathīnām ||
english: What I have deposited with the brahmin, and what among the people, and the drops that fall from the grain-offering and the goat — all that, O Agni, in the world of the well-doer, may they acknowledge us at the meeting of the paths.

sanskrit: ajaḥ pañcaudano vy akramata | tasyora iyam abhavad udaram antarikṣaṃ dyauḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ diśaḥ pārśve ||
english: The five-grain goat strode forth. This earth became its chest, the atmosphere its belly, heaven its back, and the directions its flanks.

sanskrit: ditiś cāditiś ca śṛṅge satyaṃ ca rtaṃ ca cakṣuṣī | viśvaṃ rūpaṃ śraddhā prāṇo virāṭ śiraḥ ||
english: Diti and Aditi are its two horns; truth and cosmic order are its two eyes. The all-form is its body, faith its breath, Virāj its head.

sanskrit: eṣa vā aparimito yajño yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ | aparimitaṃ lokaṃ jayaty aparimitaṃ lokam ava rundhe ya evaṃ viduṣe 'jaṃ pañcaudanaṃ dadāti ||
english: This sacrifice is indeed immeasurable — the five-grain goat offering. He wins an immeasurable world, he secures an immeasurable world, who gives a goat with the five-grain offering to one who knows thus.

sanskrit: nāsyāsthīni bhindyān na majjño nir dhayet | sarvāṇi samādāya- -idaṃidaṃ pra veśayet ||
english: One should not break its bones, nor should one drain out the marrow. Gathering all of them together, one should insert them here and here [in proper order].

sanskrit: idam idam asya rūpaṃ tenainaṃ saṃ gamayati | svadhām ūrjam akṣitiṃ maho asmai duhe ya evaṃ viduṣe 'jaṃ pañcaudanaṃ dadāti ||
english: This and this is its form; thereby one causes it to come together completely. The nourishment of the ancestral rite, strength, inexhaustibility, and greatness are milked for him who gives a goat with the five-grain offering to one who knows thus.

sanskrit: indrāya bhāgaṃ savitā kṛṇotv imaṃ yajñaṃ yajñapatiś ca sūriḥ | ye no dveṣanty anu tān rabhasva- -ariṣṭā vīrā yajamānasya sarve ||
english: May Savitṛ make the share for Indra; may the patron and lord of the sacrifice do so too. Those who hate us — seize them; may all the heroes of the sacrificer be unharmed.

sanskrit: pañca lokāḥ pañca rtavaḥ | pañcasv ṛtuṣv ṛdhnoti ya evaṃ viduṣe 'jaṃ pañcaudanaṃ dadāti ||
english: There are five worlds, five seasons. He prospers in all five seasons who gives a goat with the five-grain offering to one who knows thus.

sanskrit: eṣa vai nidāgho yajño yad ajaḥ pañcaudanaḥ | nir apriyaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ dahati bhavaty ātmanā parāsyāpriyo bhrātṛvyo bhavati (…) ||
english: This sacrifice is truly a scorching fire — the five-grain goat offering. It burns away the hateful rival; one becomes greater by virtue of oneself, and one's hateful rival becomes inferior — [and so on as the text continues].

sanskrit: yo vā āyantam ity ṛtuṃ veda | āyatīm evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya śriyam ādatte bhavaty ātmanā (…) (…) ||
english: He who knows the season called "the approaching one" — he takes away the approaching prosperity of his hateful rival; he becomes greater by virtue of himself — [remainder not preserved in this manuscript].

sanskrit: (…) vai saṃyantam iti (…) | saṃyatīm eva (…) ||
english: [He who knows the season called] "the converging one" — he takes away even the converging [prosperity of his rival — remainder not preserved in this manuscript].

sanskrit: (…) vai bhavantam iti (…) | bhavantīm eva (…) ||
english: [He who knows the season called] "the becoming one" — he takes away even the becoming [prosperity of his rival — remainder not preserved in this manuscript].

sanskrit: (…) vā abhibhavantam iti (…) | abhibhavantīm eva (…) ||
english: [He who knows the season called] "the overpowering one" — he takes away even the overpowering [prosperity of his rival — remainder not preserved in this manuscript].

sanskrit: (…) vā udyantam iti (…) | udyatīm eva (…) ||
english: [He who knows the season called] "the rising one" — he takes away even the rising [prosperity of his rival — remainder not preserved in this manuscript].

sanskrit: (…) vai mūrdhānam iti (…) | mūrdhnīm eva (…) ||
english: [He who knows the season called] "the summit" — he takes away even the summit [prosperity of his rival — remainder not preserved in this manuscript].

sanskrit: yo vai sarvam ity ṛtuṃ veda | sarvām evāpriyasya bhrātṛvyasya śriyam ādatte bhavaty ātmanā parāsyāpriyo bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ viduṣe 'jaṃ pañcaudanaṃ dadāti ||
english: He who knows the season called "the all" — he takes away the entire prosperity of his hateful rival; he becomes greater by virtue of himself, and his hateful rival becomes inferior, who gives a goat with the five-grain offering to one who knows thus.

sanskrit: yāvanty asya lomāni brahmāstṛṇoti vedyām | tāvatīr asya dhārāḥ samudrasyevākṣitāḥ ||
english: As many hairs as it has — so many the brahmin strews upon the sacrificial ground. So many are the streams that flow for him, inexhaustible as those of the ocean.

sanskrit: duhāṃ kṣīraṃ bhavatu sarpir ebhyaḥ surā bhūtvopa tiṣṭhāt surāpām | madhor dhārā madhupebhyo duhāno 'jo nāke tiṣṭhatu modamānaḥ ||
english: May it yield milk, may there be ghee for them; having become surā-liquor, may it approach the surā-drinkers. Pouring streams of mead for those who drink mead, may the goat stand on the firmament, rejoicing.
